test a different weighting scheme (softmax_neg_error) to see if a more aggressive weight on low errors improves robustness given unstable ranking.
I want to test a robust trimmed mean to see if discarding extreme model forecasts improves performance given unstable rankings and correlated errors.
The ranking is unstable (tau≈0.01) and the hint says a robust combination; median is a robust alternative to mean/trimmed mean.
Test a different kind of strategy – a DBA combination over the full pool, which may better handle unstable rankings.
try a per‑horizon best‑model weighting to capture changing winners across horizons, given the unstable ranking and strong seasonality.
The ranking is unstable and many models are correlated; a forward‑selection based weighting (w5) may pick a complementary subset.
The series has unstable rankings and strong trend/seasonality; a robust mean over a stable top‑k pool may improve performance versus full‑pool mean/weighted.
The ranking is unstable and models fall into correlated groups; a per‑horizon weighted mean on a smaller, more stable pool (pool4) might capture complementary strengths better than a full‑pool mean.
Test a weighted combination on the stable pool4 using inverse_error weights to see if a simpler weighting beats the softmax variant.
Test forward‑selection weights on full pool

decision.justification: Selected 'dba' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.9063. Series context: trend strength 1.0 and seasonal strength 1.0; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau 0.01); 2 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 0.792.
